strategy.bottleneck: [compute/mainloop-bound] The CUTLASS TF32 implicit-GEMM conv (both conv3x3 calls) is 82.9% of steady per-forward GPU time (18,433us/24 launches = 768us each; 1,536us of the 1,854us forward). Mid shape does 77.3 GFLOP per conv (M=65536,N=256,K=2304), i.e. ~100 TFLOPS on a single fixed 128x128x16 / 64x64x16 / 3-stage tile — one geometry, never tuned, only 4 warps/CTA and 8 warps/SM.
strategy.primary_optimisation_method: Mainloop tile/pipeline retune of the owned CUTLASS conv: instantiate several DefaultConv2dFprop configs (larger CTA tiles 256x128x16 and 128x256x16, deeper 4-stage 128x128x16, alternate warp partition 32x64x16 for 8 warps/CTA) and pick per problem shape via a one-time cached autotune, falling back to today's config. Directly attacks the 82.9% kernel: more warps/scheduler to hide smem->register latency and fewer CTAs re-filling activation tiles, at identical TF32 precision.
strategy.modification_plan:
1. Refactor `conv3x3_nhwc_into` into a template `template<class TB, class Warp, int Stages, int Swizzle> void conv_run(x,w,out,stream)` that instantiates exactly today's DefaultConv2dFprop (float NHWC A/B/C, OpClassTensorOp, Sm80, MMA 16x8x8, LinearCombination<float,4>, kOptimized, alpha=1,beta=0) with TB/Warp/Stages/Swizzle as parameters. No epilogue, iterator or precision change: everything stays fp32 storage + TF32 MMA + fp32 accumulate.
2. Instantiate a fixed candidate list (compile-time), each with its shared-memory budget checked against the 99KB/block limit before use:
   - C0 = 128x128x16, warp 64x64x16, stages 3  -> smem (128+128)*16*4*3 = 49KB  (current; permanent fallback)
   - C1 = 256x128x16, warp 64x64x16, stages 3  -> (256+128)*16*4*3 = 73.7KB, 8 warps/CTA
   - C2 = 128x256x16, warp 64x64x16, stages 3  -> 73.7KB, 8 warps/CTA
   - C3 = 128x128x16, warp 32x64x16, stages 4  -> (128+128)*16*4*4 = 65.5KB, 8 warps/CTA
   - C4 = 128x128x32, warp 64x64x32, stages 3  -> 98.3KB (skip if > device sharedMemPerBlockOptin)
   Query cudaDeviceGetAttribute(cudaDevAttrMaxSharedMemoryPerBlockOptin) once; drop any candidate above it. CUTLASS's initialize() already does the cudaFuncSetAttribute opt-in for >48KB.
3. Guard each candidate with `op.can_implement(args) == kSuccess`; any failure or non-success launch status removes it from the pool (never let a bad config reach the output).
4. Shape dispatch / anti-regression: compute ctas = ceil(M/TB::kM) * ceil(256/TB::kN) with M = N*H*W. Reject candidates whose ctas < 170 (one partial wave) unless C0 is also below 170; this protects the small (M=8192) and awkward (M=17161) shapes where a 256-row tile would leave <64 CTAs.
5. One-time autotune, cached: static std::map keyed by (N,H,W,C,K). On first call for a key, run each surviving candidate on the real tensors (writing to the real output buffer, idempotent since beta=0) with cudaEvent timing, 1 warmup + 3 timed reps, and store the winner index; all later calls launch only the winner. Total cost is a few hundred us on the first forward only, amortised over the benchmark loop. If timing or any launch errors, store C0.
6. Also sweep Swizzle in {1,4,8} for the winning tile only (second, cheap pass) — helps L2 locality of the K=C*R*S=2304 reduction with only 1-2 N-tiles.
7. Keep every other kernel byte-identical (nchw2nhwc, gn_partial/finalize, gn_silu, gn_silu_add_nhwc2nchw, kcrs2krsc), keep buffer reuse (z1=xh, y2=y1) and the deterministic per-chunk partials, so numerical results and the odd-HW tail behaviour are unchanged.
8. Validate on all four shapes (8x64x128, 2x64x64, 4x256x256, 1x131x131) before accepting; if the autotuned winner is not faster than C0 for a key, the cache stores C0 so the round cannot regress.
strategy.evidence: Nsight Systems: CUTLASS implicit GEMM = 82.9% steady time, 18,433us over 24 launches (768us/conv); the per-forward sum 22,245us/12 = 1,854us matches the measured 1.848ms mid-shape wall time, so 1,536us/forward is conv. Root cause: a single untuned 128x128x16 tile with 64x64 warps = only 4 warps/CTA (~8 warps/SM at 49KB smem), too few warps/scheduler to hide the fp32 smem->register + TF32 convert latency; the tile geometry was never varied. Refutation of the 'memory kernels are the bottleneck' alternative: gn_silu_add_nhwc2nchw (8.1%) is at 88.7% DRAM SOL, nchw2nhwc (4.6%) at 86.6%, gn_partial at 81.5% — all bandwidth-capped, so even zeroing every non-conv kernel caps the round at 17.1% (Amdahl).
strategy.expected_metric_change: Conv kernel gpu__time_duration down 10-25% (768us -> 580-690us per launch on the mid shape); sm__throughput / achieved TFLOPS on the conv up; sm__warps_active.avg.pct_of_peak_sustained_active for the conv up (8 warps/CTA configs); DRAM throughput of the untouched GN/transpose kernels unchanged at 81-89%. Anti-regression: candidate pool is filtered by can_implement + smem-limit + CTA-count>=170, and the per-shape cache defaults to the current 128x128x16 config, so no shape (especially 2x64x64 and 1x131x131) can be slower than today; output must stay within max_atol 0.0027-0.003 on all four shapes.

strategy.bottleneck: [memory/DRAM-bound tail around a peak-bound mainloop] The CUTLASS TF32 implicit GEMM is 84.5% of steady time but already runs 77.3 GFLOP in 784us = 98.6 TFLOPS ≈ 94% of the 104.8 TFLOPS TF32 peak, so it has no headroom. The largest remaining, actually-improvable segment is the GroupNorm moment pass: gn_partial re-reads the whole 67MB conv output from DRAM (2x per forward, 92us) at 0.34% L2 hit.
strategy.primary_optimisation_method: Producer-consumer L2 locality fusion: slice each conv into batch chunks sized to the L2 (with an L2 persisting access-policy window over the chunk's output), and launch gn_partial on each chunk immediately after its conv, so the GroupNorm moment pass reads the conv output out of L2 instead of DRAM. Metrics justify it: gn_partial is 88% DRAM SOL, 96.2% long-scoreboard stall, lts hit 0.34% — pure re-read traffic that fusion removes; the conv mainloop itself is at 94% of TF32 peak and cannot be sped up.
strategy.modification_plan:
1. Add an `int n0` parameter to gn_partial_kernel and use `const int n = n0 + blockIdx.y;` for both the input base pointer and the partial slot offset `(((size_t)n*numChunks + blockIdx.x)*G + g)*2`. Nothing else in the kernel changes, so every (n,chunk,g) slot is still written exactly once and the partial sums are bitwise identical to today (odd-HW tail behaviour preserved).
2. Split `group_moments` into `moments_partial_range(y, n0, nN, HW,C,G, part, numChunks, pixPerChunk, stream)` (launches gn_partial with `dim3 grid(numChunks, nN)` and n0) and `moments_finalize(part, mean, rstd, N*G, ...)` launched once, after all chunks, unchanged. Allocate `part` for the full N up front.
3. Give `conv3x3_nhwc_into` explicit base-pointer + N-override arguments: `conv3x3_nhwc_range(const float* xptr, const float* wptr, float* outptr, int Nsub, int H,int W,int C,int K,...)`, building Conv2dProblemSize with N=Nsub and TensorRefs from the offset pointers `xh + (size_t)n0*HW*C`, `y + (size_t)n0*HW*C`. Everything else (128x128x16 tile, kOptimized, alpha=1/beta=0) is untouched.
4. New host helper `conv_then_moments(in, w, y, N,H,W,C, part, ...)`:
   a. `size_t bytes = (size_t)N*HW*C*4;` query `cudaDeviceGetAttribute(&l2, cudaDevAttrL2CacheSize)` once (static). budget = l2/2.
   b. GATE: if `bytes <= budget || N == 1` -> single full conv + single moments_partial_range(n0=0,nN=N) (exactly today's code path; small 2x64x64 and awkward 1x131x131 shapes keep byte-identical behaviour).
   c. else `nsub = max(1, (int)(budget / ((size_t)HW*C*4)))`; raise nsub until CTAs = ceil((size_t)nsub*HW/128)*ceil(C/128) >= 170 (one full wave) so chunking never starves the grid; loop `for (n0=0; n0<N; n0+=nsub)` with `nN=min(nsub,N-n0)`: conv3x3_nhwc_range(...) then immediately moments_partial_range(y,n0,nN,...) on the SAME stream.
5. L2 persistence for the chunk: once per call do `cudaDeviceSetLimit(cudaLimitPersistingL2CacheSize, min(budget, maxPersistingL2CacheSize))`. Before each chunk's conv set `cudaStreamAttrValue v; v.accessPolicyWindow = {.base_ptr = y + (size_t)n0*HW*C, .num_bytes = min(chunkBytes, cudaDevAttrMaxAccessPolicyWindowSize), .hitRatio = 1.0f, .hitProp = cudaAccessPropertyPersisting, .missProp = cudaAccessPropertyStreaming}; cudaStreamSetAttribute(stream, cudaStreamAttributeAccessPolicyWindow, &v);` so the conv's streamed activation reads do not evict the freshly written output. After the chunk's gn_partial, set num_bytes=0 and call `cudaCtxResetPersistingL2Cache()` at the end of fused_resblock. All of this is guarded by a `#if CUDART_VERSION >= 11000` / attribute-query fallback that silently skips persistence if unsupported (correctness never depends on it).
6. Call `conv_then_moments` for BOTH convs (conv1->y1 moments, conv2->y2 moments). gn_finalize, gn_silu_nhwc, gn_silu_add_nhwc2nchw, nchw2nhwc, kcrs2krsc, buffer reuse (z1=xh, y2=y1) stay byte-identical, so this composes with every mechanism the base already carries.
7. Correctness: chunking is along the batch axis only; each output element is produced by exactly one conv call with identical problem geometry and padding, and moments are reduced over the same per-(n,chunk,g) partials, so results are bitwise unchanged. Validate all four shapes against the reference (max_atol 0.0027-0.003).
8. Anti-regression: keep a compile-time switch to force the single-shot path; if the chunked path is not faster for a shape key, the gate (bytes<=budget) already keeps small shapes on the old path.
strategy.evidence: Round-1 verdict: (ii)-by-construction — the conv does 77.3 GFLOP in 784us = 98.6 TFLOPS = 94% of the 104.8 TFLOPS TF32 peak, so a mainloop tile retune had <=6% theoretical headroom; NCU cannot profile the CUTLASS kernel here and every non-conv kernel duration in the retune profile is within 1-3% of base, so the +0.18% is unproven. New target has independent evidence: gn_partial gpu__time_duration 46,176ns x2 per forward (92us of ~1,942us), gpu__dram_throughput 87.7% of peak, lts__t_sector_hit_rate 0.34%, long_scoreboard stall 96.2% — it is a pure DRAM re-read of the 67MB conv output that was written moments earlier. Refutation of the alternative 'gn_silu_add is the bottleneck': it moves 201MB (y2+residual+out) at 88.6% DRAM SOL = 113us, which is its irreducible traffic; no fusion removes it, whereas gn_partial's 67MB read is removable outright.
strategy.expected_metric_change: gn_partial: lts__t_sector_hit_rate.pct 0.34% -> >50%, gpu__dram_throughput.avg 87.7% -> <45%, gpu__time_duration 46us -> <22us per launch on the mid shape; per-forward wall time 1.848ms -> ~1.76ms (mid) and 7.72ms -> ~7.4ms (large). Anti-regression: CUTLASS conv per-forward total must stay within 2% (chunk CTA count forced >=170), and the small (2x64x64) and awkward (1x131x131) shapes take the un-chunked gate path so their times must be unchanged; numerical output bitwise identical to the current candidate on all four shapes.

strategy.critical_issue: Persisting-L2 device limit raised once from static flag and never restored
strategy.root_cause: set_persist_window() calls cudaDeviceSetLimit(cudaLimitPersistingL2CacheSize, l2_size/2) behind a static one-shot `limit_set` flag. This is device-global, outlives forward(), and is never lowered back; reset_persist() only clears the window and cache contents, not the reservation. The harness detects the 18MB->48MB residual change after the candidate runs.
strategy.trigger_condition: Any forward() call on a device where l2_info().ok is true and the chunked path calls set_persist_window; the raised limit persists after fused_resblock returns.
must_hold_invariants: persisting L2 limit queried and restored to its prior value before forward returns
access-policy window cleared and cudaCtxResetPersistingL2Cache() called at exit
no device-global state configured from static/one-shot initializers
strategy.minimal_fix: In fused_resblock, query prior limit with cudaDeviceGetLimit(cudaLimitPersistingL2CacheSize) at entry and restore it in reset_persist(); delete the static `limit_set` one-shot guard.

strategy.bottleneck: [latency/serialization around a saturated mainloop] For the profiled mid shape the CUTLASS TF32 implicit-GEMM conv runs ~1475us of the 1848us forward at ~105 TFLOPS (=TF32 peak) while moving only ~180 GB/s, so DRAM sits ~90% idle during it; the remaining 373us is DRAM-bound GN/transpose kernels (gn_partial 92us, gn_silu_add 114us, nchw2nhwc 72us, gn_silu 69us) that run strictly serialized after it.
strategy.primary_optimisation_method: Batch-chunked two-stream pipelining: split the block along the batch axis into independent per-image chunks (GroupNorm moments are per (n,g), so chunks are fully independent) and run the whole chain conv1->partial->finalize->silu->conv2->partial2->finalize2->silu_add per chunk on two alternating CUDA streams. The compute-bound conv of one chunk then executes concurrently with the DRAM-bound GN/transpose kernels of the other, hiding most of the 373us tail behind the tensor-core-saturated conv. Purely a scheduling change; every kernel body stays byte-identical.
strategy.modification_plan:
1. Keep ALL kernels byte-identical (nchw2nhwc, gn_partial, gn_finalize, gn_silu_nhwc, gn_silu_add_nhwc2nchw, kcrs2krsc, the CUTLASS 128x128x16 conv). Only the host driver in `fused_resblock` changes: add batch-range arguments so every step can be launched on a sub-range of images.
2. Add an `int n0` parameter to gn_partial_kernel and gn_finalize_kernel launches by POINTER OFFSET instead of code change where possible: for gn_partial pass `y + (size_t)n0*HW*C` as the base and `part + (size_t)n0*numChunks*G*2` as the partial base, and launch `dim3 grid(numChunks, nSub)`; the kernel's `blockIdx.y` then indexes 0..nSub-1 relative to the offset base, so slot writes stay exactly once each (odd-HW tail unchanged). For gn_finalize launch `nSub*G` blocks with `part + n0*numChunks*G*2`, `mean + n0*G`, `rstd + n0*G`. No kernel source edits needed beyond nothing — offsets only.
3. Give the conv a range form: `conv3x3_nhwc_range(const float* a, const float* w, float* d, int Nsub,int H,int W,int C,int K, cudaStream_t s)` building Conv2dProblemSize with N=Nsub from offset pointers `xh + (size_t)n0*HW*C`, `y + (size_t)n0*HW*C`. Same tile/epilogue/precision.
4. nchw2nhwc and gn_silu_add: launch with `dim3 tgrid(ceil(HW/64), C/64, nSub)` and base pointers offset by `n0*C*HW` (NCHW side) and `n0*HW*C` (NHWC side). gn_silu_nhwc: launch `dim3(blocks, nSub)` with both tensors offset by `n0*HW*C`.
5. Chunk sizing gate (anti-regression): `ctas(c) = ceil((size_t)c*HW/128) * ceil(C/128)`. Pick the smallest `chunkN` in 1..N with `ctas(chunkN) >= 170`; `chunks = ceil(N/chunkN)`. If no such chunkN exists or `chunks < 2`, take the EXISTING single-stream path unchanged (this catches 2x64x64 -> 128 CTAs and 1x131x131 -> N=1, so those two shapes are bit-identical and time-identical to today). Mid 8x64x128 gives chunkN=2, chunks=4; large 4x256x256 gives chunkN=1, chunks=4.
6. Streams: create two `at::cuda::CUDAStream`s once via `at::cuda::getStreamFromPool()` (static, cached). At entry, record an event on the current stream after the two `to_nhwc_weight` repacks and `cudaStreamWaitEvent` it on both worker streams (weights are shared by all chunks).
7. For chunk k use `s = worker[k % 2]`; wrap all of that chunk's work in `at::cuda::CUDAStreamGuard g(s);` so the caching allocator tags the CUTLASS workspace and `part` allocations to the right stream (avoids cross-stream reuse hazards). Allocate `xh`, `y1`, `mean`, `rstd`, `part` ONCE for the full N on the main stream before the loop, and record/wait an event so both workers see them.
8. Chunk body (identical op order to today, all on `s`): nchw2nhwc(range) -> conv1(range) -> gn_partial+gn_finalize(range) -> gn_silu_nhwc(range, writes z1=xh slice) -> conv2(range) -> gn_partial+gn_finalize(range) -> gn_silu_add_nhwc2nchw(range, residual from `xc` slice). Buffer reuse (z1=xh, y2=y1) stays legal because each chunk touches only its own `n` slice.
9. Join: after the loop record an event on each worker stream and `cudaStreamWaitEvent` both on the original current stream before returning `out`; also `c10::cuda::CUDACachingAllocator::recordStream(t, s)` for `out`, `xh`, `y1`, `mean`, `rstd`, `part` so tensors allocated on the main stream but used on workers are not freed early.
10. Validate all four shapes against the reference (atol 0.0027-0.003); results are bitwise identical to today because every kernel does the same arithmetic over the same per-image data.
strategy.evidence: Mid-shape accounting: total forward 1.848ms; NCU non-conv durations sum to 373us (gn_silu_add 113.7 + gn_partial 2x46.2 + nchw2nhwc 72.4 + gn_silu 69.3 + gn_finalize 2x8.8 + kcrs 2x4.3), leaving ~1475us of conv = 154.6 GFLOP / 1475us = 105 TFLOPS ~ 100% of the 104.8 TFLOPS TF32 peak, while the conv's DRAM demand is only ~134MB/1475us ~ 180 GB/s (10% of 1792 GB/s). Root cause: two complementary resources (tensor pipe, DRAM) are used strictly one after the other. Refutation of 'the GN/transpose kernels are the bottleneck and need faster kernels': they already run at 1.86-1.94 TB/s effective (nchw2nhwc 134MB/72.4us, gn_silu 134MB/69.3us, gn_silu_add 201MB/113.7us) i.e. at or above DRAM roofline, so no rewrite of them can help — only overlapping them with the conv can. History: Round 2 targeted the same gn_partial traffic and its test FAILED, i.e. case (b) (the mechanism never engaged at all — no metric moved because nothing ran); its defect was single-stream chunking that only hoped for L2 hits and broke correctness. This proposal is mechanism-distinct (concurrency, not L2 residency), needs no cudaStreamSetAttribute/persisting-L2 machinery, and COMPOSES with every mechanism the base carries: all six kernels, the buffer reuse (z1=xh, y2=y1) and the deterministic per-chunk partials are untouched.
strategy.expected_metric_change: Mid shape wall time 1.848ms -> ~1.60-1.65ms (hiding 50-70% of the 373us serial tail); large shape 7.72ms -> ~6.9-7.2ms. gpu__dram_throughput measured DURING the conv rises from ~10% toward 50-70% (DRAM and tensor pipes busy simultaneously); per-kernel durations of gn_partial/gn_silu/nchw2nhwc individually may rise slightly (they now share bandwidth) but total forward time falls. Anti-regression: chunks<2 gate keeps 2x256x64x64 and 1x256x131x131 on the untouched single-stream path (must be within noise of today); CTA-count>=170 per chunk keeps the conv per-launch efficiency within 3% of today; numerical output bitwise identical on all four shapes.

strategy.bottleneck: [compute/latency-bound with severe wave quantization] The CUTLASS ImplicitGemmConvolution mainloop holds 89.9% of steady GPU time (31,476us / 96 launches). Its 128x128x16 tile gives only ceil(M/128) x 2 CTAs (C=256 -> 2 N-tiles), so grids land at 1.5-1.6 waves (256 and 270 CTAs vs 170 SMs) or below one wave (128 CTAs on the small shape), leaving 25-40% of SMs idle.
strategy.primary_optimisation_method: CTA tile-geometry retune of the CUTLASS conv: add a second instantiation with ThreadblockShape<128,64,16>/WarpShape<64,32,16>/4 stages (doubles N-tiles from 2 to 4, halves per-CTA accumulators to 64 regs, 12KB/stage smem -> 2 CTAs/SM) and pick per launch between it and the current 128x128x16 by wave-efficiency. This directly attacks the measured tail idle (1.5 waves -> ~3.0 waves, sub-wave grids -> 1.5 waves) without changing dtype, epilogue, or the two-stream chunk pipeline.
strategy.modification_plan:
1. Refactor `conv3x3_nhwc_range` into a template: `template<class TB, class WARP, int STAGES> struct ConvOp { using Kernel = DefaultConv2dFprop<float,TensorNHWC,...,GemmShape TB, GemmShape WARP, GemmShape<16,8,8>, LinearCombination<float,4,float,float>, GemmIdentityThreadblockSwizzle<4>, STAGES, OpMultiplyAdd, IteratorAlgorithm::kOptimized>::Kernel; using Gemm = ImplicitGemmConvolution<Kernel>; };` Keep dtype fp32/TF32 and epilogue exactly as now.
2. Instantiate exactly two configs: A = <128,128,16>/<64,64,16>/3 (today's, unchanged) and B = <128,64,16>/<64,32,16>/4. Smem budget check for B: (128+64)*16*4B = 12,288 B/stage x 4 stages = 49,152 B <= 99 KB per block, and 2 blocks/SM = 98 KB <= 100 KB per SM, so B keeps 2 CTAs/SM (A: 48 KB, 128 accum regs/thread).
3. Add `conv3x3_nhwc_range(..., int cfg)` that dispatches to A or B with identical Arguments construction (ps, TensorRefs, {1.0f,0.0f}), identical workspace handling, identical stream argument. No other kernel body changes.
4. Selection rule (host, per launch, compile-time-free): for a chunk with M = nSub*H*W, N = C: ctasA = ceil(M/128)*ceil(C/128); ctasB = ceil(M/128)*ceil(C/64). Define eff(x, slots) = x / (ceil(x/slots)*slots) with slotsA = 170 (1 CTA/SM at 128 accum regs) and slotsB = 340 (2 CTAs/SM). Choose B if eff(ctasB,slotsB) > eff(ctasA,slotsA) + 0.05 or if ctasA < 170; else keep A. Compute once per forward (shape is fixed for all chunks) and pass `cfg` down.
5. Keep the two-stream batch chunking mechanism operational (round-4 optimisation): update ONLY the chunk-size gate so `tilesN` is derived from the selected config's N-tile width (128 for A, 64 for B) instead of the hardcoded 128, i.e. `tilesN = (C + tileN - 1) / tileN;` then the existing loop `ctas = ceil(c*HW/128)*tilesN >= 170` still finds the smallest chunk that fills the GPU. Streams, events, recordStream calls and the join stay exactly as they are.
6. Leave `nchw2nhwc_kernel`, `gn_partial_kernel`, `gn_finalize_kernel`, `gn_silu_nhwc_kernel`, `gn_silu_add_nhwc2nchw_kernel`, `kcrs2krsc_kernel` byte-identical, so GroupNorm reduction order (and numerics) is unchanged and the awkward-shape tail handling stays correct.
7. Numerics: both configs use the same TF32 MMA (16,8,8) and fp32 accumulate; only tile/warp partition of the K-loop reduction changes, which stays within the 2.8e-3 atol contract already met by config A.
8. Guard: `TORCH_CHECK(op.can_implement(args) == Success)` on both paths; if B reports unsupported for a given problem (should not happen: C=256 and alignment-4 satisfied), fall back to A at runtime.
9. Validation checklist: run all four scored shapes; expected grids after the change — mid chunk M=16384 -> B: 128*4 = 512 CTAs / 340 slots = 1.5 waves per SM-pair (vs A 256/170 = 1.51 waves at 1 CTA/SM but with 33% tail); awkward N=1 M=17161 -> B: 135*4 = 540 vs A 270; small N=2 M=8192 -> B: 64*4 = 256 CTAs vs A 128 (sub-wave). Keep whichever config the rule picks per shape.
10. Anti-regression: if the large shape (4x256x256x256, A already at 6 waves, eff ~0.99) selects B and slows down, the eff+0.05 margin keeps A — verify the rule returns A there.
strategy.evidence: Conv = 89.9% steady time, 31,476us over 96 launches; per-forward conv work sums to ~2.6ms while wall time is 1.613ms (streams overlap), i.e. ~59 TFLOPS vs 104.8 TF32 peak = 56% of peak. Root cause: with C=256 the 128-wide N-tile yields only 2 N-tiles, so grids are 256 CTAs (mid chunk) and 270 CTAs (awkward shape) against 170 SMs = 1.5-1.6 waves (33-41% tail idle), and 128 CTAs (small shape) never fills the GPU. Refutation of DRAM-bound alternative: each conv launch moves ~18-26MB for ~2-4e10 FLOP (<100 GB/s required at peak vs 1792 GB/s available); the genuinely DRAM-saturated kernels (85% DRAM throughput) are the GN/transpose kernels, which together are only ~10% of steady time.
strategy.expected_metric_change: (1) CUTLASS conv total GPU time drops 10-25% (31,476us -> <28,000us) and its steady share falls below 89%; (2) conv grid size per launch rises from 256 to 512 CTAs (mid chunk) / 128 to 256 (small shape), pushing achieved occupancy and sm__throughput on the conv up while wave tail idle falls; (3) launch__occupancy_limit_registers for the conv improves (64 vs 128 accumulator regs/thread -> 2 blocks/SM). Anti-regression constraints: kernel launch count must stay 456 (no extra kernels, chunking gate still splits into >=2 chunks so the two-stream conv/GN overlap remains visible in the nsys timeline — if chunks collapses to 1 the round-4 pipelining is silently lost); GN kernel timings and numerics unchanged; the large 4x256x256x256 shape must not regress (rule must select config A there).

strategy.bottleneck: [DRAM/overlap-bound residual, conv already at roofline] CUTLASS conv holds 89.6% steady time but 2 convs = 1.546e11 FLOP vs 104.8 TF32 TFLOPS = 1.475 ms floor against a 1.613 ms wall, i.e. ~91% of SOL. The remaining ~140 us is the un-hidden DRAM traffic of nchw2nhwc / gn_partial / gn_silu* (DRAM 80-87%, L2 hit 0.7-2%), plus small/awkward shapes where the chunk gate disables pipelining entirely.
strategy.primary_optimisation_method: L2-residency chunk sizing of the existing two-stream batch pipeline: pick chunkN from the runtime l2CacheSize so that the per-chunk working set of both in-flight streams fits L2, and lower the CTA-fill threshold from 170 to ~85 CTAs per stream (two streams jointly fill the GPU) so chunks>=2 also on N=2. GN kernels then read conv output from L2 instead of DRAM (lts hit 0.7-1.9% today) and stop stealing bandwidth from the conv; the small shape gains conv/GN overlap it currently never gets.
strategy.modification_plan:
Host-driver-only change in fused_resblock; every __global__ body stays byte-identical, so GroupNorm reduction order and numerics are bit-identical.

1. Query L2 once: `static int L2B = [](){cudaDeviceProp p; cudaGetDeviceProperties(&p, 0); return p.l2CacheSize;}();` (never hardcode; falls back to 64MB if 0).
2. Replace the current gate (`smallest c with ceil(c*HW/128)*tilesN >= 170`) with a two-part rule:
   a. FILL: `ctas(c) = ((long)c*HW + 127)/128 * ((C+127)/128)`; pick `cfill` = smallest c in [1,N] with `ctas(c) >= 85` (half the 170 SMs, because two worker streams run concurrently); if none, `cfill = N`.
   b. L2: per chunk the live bytes are 4 full-tensor slices (x slice read, xh, y1, out slice) = `4*(size_t)c*HW*C*4`. Two chunks are in flight, so require `2*live(c) <= 0.60*L2B`; let `cl2` = largest c satisfying it, min 1. Set `chunkN = max(1, min(cfill, cl2))`.
3. OVERLAP CLAUSE: if `N >= 2 && (N + chunkN - 1)/chunkN < 2`, set `chunkN = N/2` (>=1) so at least two chunks exist and the two-stream pipeline actually engages. This is what fixes 2x256x64x64, where today `ctas(c)=c*64 < 170` for all c<=2 so `chunkN=0` and `pipelined=false` (single stream, zero conv/GN overlap).
4. Keep `chunks = (N + chunkN - 1)/chunkN;  pipelined = (chunks >= 2);` and the entire event/record_stream/join structure untouched, so the round-4 stream_pipeline_overlap mechanism is preserved, not replaced.
5. Keep numChunks/pixPerChunk for GroupNorm computed from the FULL batch exactly as now (they are per-image quantities), so the partial buffer layout, the empty-chunk zero-fill tail handling for odd HW (131x131), and the reduction order are unchanged -> identical outputs.
6. Keep the CUTLASS config at <128,128,16>/<64,64,16>/3 stages (round-5 retune regressed; do not touch tile geometry).
7. Reduce per-chunk workspace churn: hoist the CUTLASS workspace allocation out of `conv3x3_nhwc_range` into a single `torch::empty` sized for the largest chunk, allocated once per forward on the main stream and record_stream'd to both workers, passed in as a pointer (avoids 2*chunks allocator calls now that chunk count roughly doubles).
8. Expected launch/geometry effect on the profiled mid shape: chunkN 2 -> 1, chunks 4 -> 8, per-chunk live bytes 4*8.4MB = 33.6MB, both streams 67MB; if that exceeds 0.60*L2B the rule keeps chunkN=2 automatically, so the change is self-limiting.
9. Large shape 4x256x256x256: `live(1) = 4*67MB = 268MB > 0.6*L2B` -> `cl2 = 1`, `cfill = 1` (ctas=1024) -> chunkN stays 1, chunks stays 4: bit-identical schedule, no regression path.
10. Awkward shape 1x256x131x131: N=1 -> chunkN=1, chunks=1, pipelined=false, unchanged behaviour (vec=0 path preserved).
11. Validation: run all four scored shapes; assert output allclose to reference (atol 2.8e-3) and that nsys shows >=2 concurrent streams for N>=2 shapes.
strategy.evidence: Round-5 classification = (a): the predicted metric DID move (conv N-tiles 2->4, grid 256->512 CTAs) yet all four shapes regressed (-0.4/-2.3/-0.2/-0.0%), so the wave-quantization model was wrong; the deciding number is the roofline: 2 convs = 1.546e11 FLOP / 104.8 TF32 TFLOPS = 1.475 ms vs 1.613 ms measured wall = ~91% of SOL, leaving ~9% total headroom, none of it inside the conv math. Root cause of that residual: the GN/transpose kernels run at 80-87% DRAM throughput with lts__t_sector_hit_rate 0.68/1.36/1.94/1.72% - every inter-kernel handoff (67MB tensors) goes to DRAM and competes with the conv. Refuted alternative: 'conv tail idle' (already disproved above) and 'gn_partial occupancy' (16% achieved occupancy, but it is at 70.7% DRAM with 2.5% SM throughput, so it is bandwidth- not occupancy-limited). Round-5 broke nothing structurally (launch count and overlap intact); this plan composes with stream_pipeline_overlap by re-tuning only its chunk-size gate and explicitly widens it to N=2 where the gate currently disables it.
strategy.expected_metric_change: (1) lts__t_sector_hit_rate on gn_partial/gn_silu_nhwc/gn_silu_add rises from ~1-2% to >20%, and their gpu__dram_throughput falls below 70% (traffic served from L2). (2) 2x256x64x64 gains conv/GN overlap: nsys must show >=2 concurrent streams and >=2 chunks (today chunkN=0 -> pipelined=false), with its speedup rising above 1.15x. (3) Total per-forward wall drops toward the 1.475 ms conv roofline (mid shape <1.58 ms). Anti-regression constraints: 4x256x256x256 must keep chunkN=1/chunks=4 and its kernel schedule unchanged (its speedup must stay >=1.33x); the two-stream mechanism must remain visible (if the timeline shows a single stream, the gate broke); kernel launch count may rise at most ~2x on the mid shape and must not push CPU launch time above GPU time on the small shape; outputs must stay bit-identical to the current base (same GN reduction order).

strategy.bottleneck: [DRAM/latency-bound satellite segment] The GroupNorm moment path (gn_partial + gn_finalize) around the near-roofline CUTLASS conv: 4.7% of steady GPU time and 192 of 456 launches. gn_partial runs only 64 CTAs (0.06 waves/SM, 16.2% occupancy) so it reaches just 70.7% DRAM vs 85-87% for sibling streaming kernels; gn_finalize is pure launch latency (0.55% DRAM, 0.03 waves).
strategy.primary_optimisation_method: atomic_privatize the GroupNorm moment reduction: one grid-filling kernel per chunk whose blocks privatize (sum, sumsq) per group in shared memory, atomically combine into per-(n,g) accumulators, and let the last-arriving block per (n,g) finalize mean/rstd. This deletes the second launch entirely and lets the moment pass use ~680 CTAs instead of 64, converting a 16%-occupancy, 70%-DRAM read into a bandwidth-saturated one. Matches the measured evidence (long-scoreboard 86.6% with 1.95 active warps/scheduler = not enough memory parallelism in flight).
strategy.modification_plan:
Host driver + two GN kernels only; CUTLASS conv, nchw2nhwc, gn_silu_nhwc, gn_silu_add_nhwc2nchw stay byte-identical, so stream_pipeline_overlap (round 4) remains fully operational (per-chunk pointer offsets, worker streams, events, recordStream unchanged).

1. Replace `gn_partial_kernel` + `gn_finalize_kernel` with ONE kernel `gn_moments_kernel(y, acc, cnt_ctr, mean, rstd, HW, C, G, Cg, pixPerBlock, blocksPerImage, cnt, eps)`. Delete both old kernels and the two launches in `group_moments_range`; `group_moments_range` now issues exactly one launch per call (96 -> 48 GN-reduction launches per profile run; total launches 456 -> ~372).
2. Kernel body (keeps the existing vectorized float4 access pattern verbatim): tpp = C>>2, ppp = 256/tpp; block (bx, n) covers pixels [bx*pixPerBlock, min(HW,(bx+1)*pixPerBlock)); each thread accumulates s, ss over float4 loads; store to __shared__ sms[256]/smss[256]; __syncthreads(); threads 0..G-1 fold their group's lanes exactly as today into ts, tss.
3. Combine with atomics instead of a second kernel: `atomicAdd(&acc[(n*G+g)*2], ts); atomicAdd(&acc[(n*G+g)*2+1], tss);` then `__threadfence();` and, from thread 0 of the block, `old = atomicAdd(&ctr[n], 1)`; the block that observes `old == blocksPerImage-1` re-reads acc for all G groups of image n and writes mean/rstd with the SAME double-precision formula the old finalize used (m = s/cnt; v = max(0, ss/cnt - m*m); rstd = 1/sqrt(v+eps)). Consumers (`gn_silu_nhwc_kernel`, `gn_silu_add_nhwc2nchw_kernel`) keep reading mean[]/rstd[] unchanged — no per-element double math is introduced.
4. Buffers: allocate once per forward `acc` = 2 (stages) * N*G*2 floats and `ctr` = 2*N ints, and zero BOTH with a single `cudaMemsetAsync` on the main stream before `start_ev.record(main_stream)`, so both worker streams already wait on it; recordStream them to both workers like `part` today. Stage 1 uses slot 0, stage 2 slot 1, so no inter-stage re-zero and no extra launch inside the chunk loop. Drop the old `part` tensor and its numChunks/pixPerChunk math.
5. Grid sizing (this is the fix for the 0.06-wave launch): `blocksPerImage = clamp(ceil((long)HW / (long)ppp), 1, max(1, 680 / max(nSub,1)))` refined as: target total CTAs ~= 4*170 = 680 across the (blocksPerImage, nSub) grid, but never more blocks than pixel-passes available, i.e. `blocksPerImage = min(ceil(HW/(ppp*4)), ceil(680/nSub))`, minimum 1. Then `pixPerBlock = ceil(HW/blocksPerImage)` and recompute `blocksPerImage = ceil(HW/pixPerBlock)` so NO launched block is empty — this makes the atomic counter target exactly equal to the launched block count and removes the unwritten-tail class of bug that bit run D on odd HW (131x131, HW=17161 is handled because pixPerBlock is a ceiling and the last block is simply short).
6. Numerics: block partials are still fp32 sums of >=1024 elements; only the ~blocksPerImage-way final combine becomes atomic (nondeterministic order). Relative error on mean/rstd stays ~1e-6, far inside the 2.8e-3 atol contract. Keep the double-precision finalize arithmetic to avoid cancellation in ss/cnt - m*m.
7. Accounting for what is removed: gn_finalize_kernel is deleted; its function (per-(n,g) mean/rstd) is subsumed by the last-block path in step 3, so no behaviour is lost. No listed base mechanism is disabled: chunking, two worker streams, events and joins are untouched.
8. Validation: run all four scored shapes; assert allclose(atol 2.8e-3); confirm in nsys that (a) gn_finalize no longer appears, (b) two concurrent worker streams still appear for N>=2 shapes, (c) conv kernel time/launch count unchanged (96).
strategy.evidence: gn_partial: 1351us steady (3.9%), 13.5us/launch, launch__grid_size=64, waves_per_multiprocessor=0.06, achieved occupancy 16.2%, DRAM 70.7% while nchw2nhwc/gn_silu_add on the same tensors hit 84.9-87.1% — it is under-filled, not bandwidth-limited (long_scoreboard 86.6% with only 1.95 active warps/scheduler = insufficient loads in flight). gn_finalize: 273us, 64 CTAs, 0.03 waves, DRAM 0.55% = pure launch/latency. Prior round-6 classification = (b): it predicted lts__t_sector_hit_rate >20% on the GN kernels; measured 1.48/1.93/1.76% — the L2-residency mechanism never engaged, so scheduling/L2 tuning is not the lever; this plan instead removes a launch and fixes memory-level parallelism, and composes with stream_pipeline_overlap (host loop untouched). Refuted alternative: the CUTLASS conv (88.3%) — 1.546e11 FLOP / 104.8 TF32 TFLOPS = 1.475ms vs 1.613ms wall, and two direct conv retunes (rounds 5, 6) regressed, so conv math is not the accessible headroom.
strategy.expected_metric_change: (1) gn_moments_kernel launch__grid_size rises 64 -> ~680 CTAs, waves_per_multiprocessor 0.06 -> ~1.0, achieved occupancy 16.2% -> >60%, gpu__dram_throughput 70.7% -> >85%, kernel duration 13.5us -> <11us per launch. (2) gn_finalize_kernel disappears (273us and 96 launches removed); total forward launch count 456 -> ~372. Anti-regression: conv launch count stays 96 and its per-launch duration unchanged; nsys must still show two concurrent worker streams on N>=2 shapes (loss would mean the memset/event ordering broke pipelining); outputs allclose at atol 2.8e-3 on all four shapes, especially 1x256x131x131 where blocksPerImage must equal the atomic counter target (no empty blocks, no unwritten tail); small shape 2x256x64x64 must improve (fewer launches), not regress.
